verdicts.quote: The promoted member is booked without accepting, confirming or claiming anything, and without any time limit running against them.
Members A, B and C join the same waitlist in that order. A is at position 1, B at position 2, C at position 3.
verdicts.missing: How simultaneous joins are ordered (C-29 only requires distinct positions), and whether any membership tier or staff override can jump the queue.

verdicts.quote: A, B waiting; a spot opens; A would be refused by an existing booking rule. A is not booked and is no longer waiting. B is booked.
verdicts.missing: Whether promotion into one class removes or keeps the member's entry on an overlapping class's waitlist; the clash rule is only an example of rules that may exist today.

verdicts.quote: Their bookings show the class as booked as soon as a spot opens and they next look.
If the app sends a member a message when they book a class, a promoted member gets a message of the same kind saying they have been booked in the class.
verdicts.missing: What happens when sending the notification fails.

verdicts.quote: Two booked members cancel at the same moment. A and B are booked, each once, and C is at position 1. The class is 10/10.
A member waiting in a class is booked into it in a way that is not promotion (for instance by staff). They are shown as booked, they are not shown as waiting for it
verdicts.missing: The race where a waitlisted member books directly at the same moment they are promoted; only sequential cases and the general one-booking rule (C-40) are stated.

verdicts.quote: a floor of 100 is fixed and no refusal for length is required below it
verdicts.missing: Whether there is any cap above 100 and what a member sees if the waitlist is full.

verdicts.quote: A class started at 18:00 with member A waiting. A booked member cancels at 18:05. A is not booked... the cutoff follows the existing rule for when a class can no longer be booked
Staff raise a class's capacity from 10 to 13 while 5 members wait: the first 3 in line are booked, and the other 2 are at positions 1 and 2.
verdicts.missing: What happens when staff lower capacity while a waitlist exists.

verdicts.quote: A class with 3 waiting members is cancelled or deleted. None of the 3 is booked into it, and none sees it as a class they are waiting for.
Waitlist order is order of joining
verdicts.missing: The waitlist entry's recorded fields (join time, state) and whether position is stored or derived.

verdicts.quote: After a class has started, members who had been waiting for it do not see it listed as one they are still waiting for.
verdicts.missing: Whether the entries are deleted or kept, and for how long.

verdicts.quote: A member waiting at position 3 in a class sees, among their own classes, that they are waiting for it and that their position is 3.
verdicts.missing: Whether members can or cannot see the identities of others on the waitlist.

verdicts.quote: For a class with A, B, C waiting, staff see the waiting members as A, B, C in that order, apart from the booked members.
verdicts.missing: Staff removing someone from the waitlist by hand, and a record of who was promoted and when.

verdicts.quote: A booked member cancels and A is booked, making the class 10/10 again. Member X, who is not waiting, tries to book that class and finds it full
For a class with an empty waitlist, listing, booking, cancelling and the free-spot count behave as before the waitlist existed.
Right after the upgrade, every class (including any that is full) has no one waiting. A member can join the waitlist of a full class and gets position 1.
